chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Al-Abbas, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What is for the man he can punish his slave with?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'According to the measure of his sin.' I said, 'So you punished Hareez with greater than his crime.' He said, 'Woe to you! He was a slave of mine, and Hareez brandished the sword, and the one who brandished the sword is not from me.'

key_terms.حَرِيز: Hareez (a specific slave of the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What is the principle for punishing a slave in Shia jurisprudence according to the Imams?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the general principle of proportional retribution for slaves, but uses the case of Hareez to illustrate that context and status modify the severity of punishment. The Imam distinguishes between a mere slave and one who 'brandishes the sword,' implying that Hareez’s act carried the weight of a challenge to authority or a threat of rebellion, thus justifying a harsher penalty than the literal crime might suggest. This highlights the Shia juristic understanding that punishment is not merely mechanical but considers the social and hierarchical implications of the act.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, from Abu Al Abbas who said,
